claims.claim: Spain has a non-lucrative residence visa, and its holders may not work

sources.name: Spanish Consulate General in Los Angeles: non-lucrative residence visa
sources.says: Dated February 11, 2026. The visa is for residing in Spain without carrying out any gainful (work or professional) activity: "This visa does not constitute a work permit." and "This type of visa does not allow teleworking."

sources.name: Spanish Consulate General in London: non-lucrative residence visa
sources.says: Dated July 6, 2026. Residence "without carrying out any gainful (work or professional) activity"; "This visa does not constitute a work permit."

claims.note: The golden visa is not mentioned in any Spain profile, so its end (April 2025) is not a claim here and was not checked.

claims.claim: The visa needs €2,400 a month or €28,800 a year, which is 400% of the 2026 IPREM

sources.name: Spanish Consulate General in Los Angeles: non-lucrative residence visa
sources.says: "The minimum required amount is equivalent to 400% of Spain's Public Multiple Effects Income Indicator" (IPREM). The page gives no euro amount; it links to an IPREM document. Dated February 11, 2026.

sources.name: SEPE (state employment service): Cuantías anuales
sources.says: The table of yearly amounts gives the IPREM for 2026 as 600,00 € a month and 7.200,00 € a year, citing Ley 31/2022 (the 2023 budget law, still extended).

sources.name: Costa Luz Lawyers: IPREM 2026 for the non-lucrative visa
sources.says: IPREM €600 a month, €7,200 a year, "unchanged from 2025"; the main applicant must show 400% of the annual IPREM, €28,800 a year (about €2,400 a month). The page carries no date (footer © 2025) and its FAQ says the 2026 IPREM had not yet been published; two of its examples use other amounts (€31,680 and €39,600).

also: sources: S.iprem (Costa Luz Lawyers) replaced inline in all seven profiles by the SEPE table of yearly amounts and the Los Angeles consulate's visa page; the Costa Luz page has the right headline figures but is undated, says the 2026 IPREM is not yet published and contradicts itself in two examples
claims.note: The euro figures are 4 × the official IPREM: 4 × €600 = €2,400 a month and 4 × €7,200 = €28,800 a year. No official page read states the product in euros. The Ministry of Inclusion's own information sheet (https://www.inclusion.gob.es/en/web/migraciones/w/autorizacion-inicial-de-residencia-temporal-no-lucrativa) returned HTTP 403. Valencia's first drawback repeats €2,400/month and compares it with Portugal's €920 (checked in portugal.json).

claims.claim: Each dependant adds €7,200 a year (100% of IPREM)

sources.name: Spanish Consulate General in Los Angeles: non-lucrative residence visa
sources.says: "To this amount, must be added 100% of the IPREM for each family member."

sources.name: SEPE (state employment service): Cuantías anuales
sources.says: IPREM for 2026: 7.200,00 € a year (600,00 € a month).

claims.claim: The means may be investment income or liquid savings

sources.name: Spanish Consulate General in Los Angeles: non-lucrative residence visa
sources.says: The applicant must prove "sufficient financial means to cover the expenses of residing in Spain for the initial year of the residence permit or accrediting that they have a regular source of income". Retirees must have a state pension or a non-capitalizable life annuity "in convertible currency and / or investment accounts"; bank statements for three months, year-end and average balances and the last tax return are required. The page also says: "Residency applicants cannot have/leave loans or mortgages in the United States when applying for residency in Spain."

sources.name: Spanish Consulate General in London: non-lucrative residence visa
sources.says: Requires "original and stamped documents that verify the perception of a periodic and sufficient income or the holding of an estate that guarantees the perception of that income", with bank balances at 31 December and the year's average balance.

claims.note: Both routes are on the official pages: a regular income, or funds for the year. Not in the profiles, and worth the user's eye for a buy-borrow-die reader: the Los Angeles consulate says applicants cannot have or leave loans or mortgages in the United States. The London page has no such line; whether a margin loan counts, and whether other US consulates apply it, was not established. Added to the seven profiles after the plan at the user's call: see es-visa-la-no-us-loans.

claims.claim: The Los Angeles consulate says non-lucrative visa applicants "cannot have/leave loans or mortgages in the United States", without saying whether a margin loan counts

sources.name: Spanish Consulate General in Los Angeles: non-lucrative residence visa
sources.says: In the financial-means section, after "Attach bank statements from the last three months and a copy of the last tax return": "Residency applicants cannot have/leave loans or mortgages in the United States when applying for residency in Spain." No type of loan is named and no explanation is given.

claims.note: Added after the fact check at the user's call (the report's question 4). The London consulate's page has no such line; whether other US consulates apply it was not established.

claims.claim: The visa needs Spanish private health insurance with no co-pay

sources.name: Spanish Consulate General in Los Angeles: non-lucrative residence visa
sources.says: The policy must have "no deductible, no copayment, no waiting period or coverage limit", cover all beneficiaries for one year and be "contracted with an insurance entity authorized to operate in Spain"; "No travel insurances with medical assistance coverage will be accepted."

sources.name: Spanish Consulate General in London: non-lucrative residence visa
sources.says: Insurance from an insurer authorized in Spain that "must cover all the risks insured by Spain's public health system".

claims.claim: Holders must live in Spain most of the year

sources.name: The Local Spain: Spain clarifies 183-day rule for digital nomad visa renewals
sources.says: Dated 29 June 2026. The Supreme Court ruling for other permits does not reach the non-lucrative visa: under Article 64 f) of Royal Decree 1155/2024 a renewal needs "real and effective residence in Spain for more than 183 days during each calendar year".

sources.name: Costa Luz Lawyers: Can you renew your Spanish residency without spending 183 days in Spain?
sources.says: Posted 23 June 2026, updated 3 October 2026. Article 64.2(f) of the Immigration Regulation requires more than 183 days of real and effective residence in each calendar year to renew a non-lucrative permit; the Supreme Court judgments on absences (STS 731/2023 and later) do not automatically remove it, and holders "should assume that the requirement remains fully applicable when renewing".

claims.note: Secondary pages: the Ministry of Inclusion's renewal sheet returned HTTP 403 (www.inclusion.gob.es), connection refused (accesible.inclusion.gob.es) and a certificate error (the PDF on ciudadaniaexterior.inclusion.gob.es). The rule is a renewal condition, and it is being argued over in the courts; one page found by search, not read, reports a lawyer saying renewal is now possible without 183 days.

claims.claim: Spain taxes a resident's worldwide net wealth

sources.name: PwC: Spain, other taxes
sources.says: "Wealth tax is levied on Spanish tax residents' worldwide net assets", measured at 31 December; regions may set their own exempt minimum, scale and reliefs. Last reviewed 30 June 2026.

sources.name: Agencia Tributaria: Manual práctico de Patrimonio 2025, sujetos pasivos por obligación personal
sources.says: Residents must declare all assets and rights held at 31 December "con independencia del lugar donde se encuentren situados los bienes o puedan ejercitarse los derechos", less charges and personal debts.

claims.note: Agrees with the regional entries in src/data/localTaxes.ts (wealth base "net").

claims.claim: Margin debt is deductible from the wealth-tax base

sources.name: Agencia Tributaria: Manual práctico de Patrimonio 2025, deudas deducibles
sources.says: Deductible: "las deudas y obligaciones personales de las que deba responder el sujeto pasivo", duly justified, at nominal value on 31 December; interest is never deductible, and debts taken on to acquire exempt assets are not deductible.

claims.note: The page states the general rule for personal debts and does not name margin loans. A margin loan against a taxable portfolio is a personal debt of the taxpayer; one used to buy an exempt asset would not be deductible.

claims.claim: The Valencian Community exempts the first €2M of net wealth from the 2026 assessment, under Ley 5/2026

sources.name: Generalitat Valenciana (Hisenda): Beneficios fiscales 2026
sources.says: "Beneficios fiscales 2026": for taxpayers habitually resident in the Comunitat Valenciana the taxable base "se reduce, en concepto de mínimo exento, en 2.000.000€" (Art. 8 Llei 13/1997). No general bonificación is listed for the tax.

sources.name: Cuatrecasas: Comunidad Valenciana, novedades tributarias para 2026
sources.says: Dated 18 August 2026. Ley 5/2026, de 31 de julio (DOGV 10 August 2026, in force 11 August) raises the mínimo exento from 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 euros for resident taxpayers, "con efectos prácticos desde el 31 de diciembre de 2026", i.e. in the 2026 return filed in 2027. Ley 5/2025 had raised it from 500,000.

sources.name: Garrigues: Comunidad Valenciana, novedades en los tributos autonómicos para 2026 y 2027
sources.says: Dated 4 September 2026. "Ahora se duplica este umbral hasta los 2.000.000 de euros, con efectos ya para 2026." No change to the rate scale is mentioned.

also: sources: added the Generalitat Valenciana's "Beneficios fiscales 2026" page to Valencia, Alicante and Torrevieja
claims.note: Agrees with ES_VALENCIA in src/data/localTaxes.ts (€2M exemption). The Generalitat's older wealth-tax page (atv.gva.es/es/ipatrimoni) was reported by search, not read, as still showing €1,000,000; the Agencia Tributaria's 2025 manual shows €1,000,000 because it covers the 2025 assessment. The summaries of all three profiles, their first or second drawback ("above €2M") and the `why` lines of Valencia, Alicante and Torrevieja repeat the €2M figure correctly.

claims.claim: Above the exemption the Valencian scale runs from 0.25% to 3.5%, with no general relief

sources.name: Agencia Tributaria: Manual práctico de Patrimonio 2025, escala autonómica de la Comunitat Valenciana
Guía Fiscal: Patrimonio 2026, mapa de bonificaciones por comunidad
sources.says: Comunitat Valenciana: mínimo exento 2,000,000 € from the 31 December 2026 accrual; bonificación 0% (the region does not relieve the tax "con carácter general"); scale 0.25% to 3.5%. Page marked reviewed 17 May 2026, though it cites the law of 31 July 2026.

claims.note: The scale is the 2025 one; Garrigues (4 September 2026, see es-tax-valencia-exemption-2m) reports no change to it for 2026. Agrees bracket for bracket with ES_VALENCIA in src/data/localTaxes.ts (0.25, 0.37, 0.62, 1.12, 1.62, 2.12, 2.62, 3.5 on the state breakpoints). scores.tax stays 2: a wealth tax above a high threshold.

claims.claim: The income-plus-wealth cap can cut the wealth tax by up to 80%

sources.name: Agencia Tributaria: Manual práctico de Patrimonio 2025, límite de cuota íntegra, reglas
sources.says: "Si se produjera un exceso del límite del 60 por 100, dicho exceso deberá ser reducido en la cuota" of the wealth tax, "sin que la reducción pueda exceder del 80 por 100 de dicha cuota", leaving a "cuota mínima no reducible ... equivalente al 20 por 100".

claims.note: The limit is 60% of the income-tax base for the two taxes together (art. 31 of the wealth tax law). Málaga's and Madrid's profiles do not mention it; it applies there too. Agrees with ES_CAP in src/data/localTaxes.ts, which names the cap and does not model it.

claims.claim: Dividends and interest pay 19–30%

sources.name: PwC: Spain, taxes on personal income
sources.says: Savings income (dividends, interest, capital gains): 19% on the first EUR 6,000; 21% to EUR 50,000; 23% to EUR 200,000; 27% to EUR 300,000; 30% above. Last reviewed 30 June 2026.

sources.name: Agencia Tributaria: Manual práctico de Renta 2025, gravamen estatal de la base liquidable del ahorro
Agencia Tributaria: Manual práctico de Renta 2025, gravamen autonómico de la base liquidable del ahorro
sources.says: Regional scale "para 2025": the same five brackets at 9.5%, 10.5%, 11.5%, 13.5% and 15%, so the two together give 19%, 21%, 23%, 27% and 30%.

claims.note: The 30% top rate starts above €300,000 of savings income; most retirees' dividends fall in the 19–23% brackets. Not claims in the profiles, read for context: PwC's "other issues" page says the special expatriate (Beckham) regime needs an employment contract, a directorship, remote work, entrepreneurial activity or a qualifying professional role, so it does not reach a retiree; PwC's treaties page lists a US treaty and a deduction for foreign tax on foreign-source income. The US–Spain treaty's withholding caps were not read, and no profile states them.

claims.claim: Foreign assets are reported on Modelo 720

sources.name: Agencia Tributaria: Modelo 720, declaración informativa sobre bienes y derechos situados en el extranjero
sources.says: "Declaración Informativa. Declaración sobre bienes y derechos situados en el extranjero", approved by Orden HAP/72/2013; virtual currencies are not reported on it.

sources.name: Agencia Tributaria: Modelo 720, preguntas frecuentes, contribuyentes obligados a declarar
sources.says: The form must be filed by "las personas físicas residentes en territorio español", among others; people under the special regime for displaced workers are excused.

sources.name: Agencia Tributaria: Modelo 720, preguntas frecuentes, forma de calcular el límite
sources.says: Its examples turn on 50.000 €: an account with "saldo medio 4T superior a 50.000 €", a fund with "valor liquidativo a 31/12 superior a 50.000 €".

claims.note: The €50,000-per-category threshold appears on the official pages only through examples; the profiles do not state it.

claims.claim: An exit tax can reach gains on shares worth over €4M

sources.name: Agencia Tributaria: Manual práctico de Renta 2025, ganancias patrimoniales por cambio de residencia
sources.says: The regime applies when the market value of the shares or participations "exceda, conjuntamente, de 4.000.000 euros"; failing that, when a holding above 25% of an entity is worth more than 1.000.000 de euros.

claims.note: Five profiles omit the residence condition (see es-tax-exit-tax-10-years); what they say is still true. The €1M / 25% alternative is not in the profiles.

claims.claim: The exit tax applies after 10 years' residence

sources.name: Agencia Tributaria: Manual práctico de Renta 2025, ganancias patrimoniales por cambio de residencia
sources.says: The taxpayer must have been resident "durante al menos diez de los quince períodos impositivos anteriores" to the last period to be declared.

claims.note: Ten of the last fifteen tax years, not ten years in a row.

claims.claim: Andalusia's 100% relief means no wealth tax is due below about €3.7M of net wealth; above that the region collects about the solidarity-tax rates, 1.7–3.5%

sources.name: Agencia Tributaria: Manual práctico de Patrimonio 2025, bonificaciones autonómicas, Andalucía
sources.says: Under the disposición transitoria quinta of Ley 5/2021, from 2024 and while the ITSGF is in force the general bonus of article 25 bis "(del 100 por 100)" is not applicable; the taxpayer may apply a bonus equal to the difference, if any, between the wealth-tax quota and the ITSGF quota, each after its joint limit.

sources.name: PwC: Spain, other taxes
sources.says: Solidarity tax: applies to net assets "equal to or higher than EUR 3 million"; the EUR 700,000 exemption applies; rates 0% to 3,000,000, 1.7% to 5,347,998.03, 2.1% to 10,695,996.06, 3.5% above; wealth tax paid is deducted from it. Last reviewed 30 June 2026.

sources.name: Cuatrecasas: Medidas adoptadas ante el Impuesto sobre las grandes fortunas
sources.says: Dated 26 March 2026. Large fortunes for the ITSGF are those "superior a 3.700.000€". In Andalusia the taxpayer's option of 2023 has gone: for 2024 onward "se ha suprimido la mecánica de la opción" and the tax is collected under the wealth tax.

sources.name: Agencia Tributaria: Manual práctico de Patrimonio 2025, escala autonómica de Andalucía
sources.says: Eight brackets from 0.20% to 3.50% on the state breakpoints (1.70% from 2,673,999.01; 2.10% from 5,347,998.03; 3.50% from 10,695,996.06).

claims.note: How it works: the 100% bonus is formally suspended while the solidarity tax exists and replaced by a bonus of the wealth-tax quota minus the solidarity-tax quota, so a resident pays the region exactly what the solidarity tax would have charged: nothing until the base passes €3M after the €700k exempt minimum (about €3.7M of net wealth), then 1.7%, 2.1% and 3.5%. The profile's "100% relief" is loose but its effect and figures are right; the summary, the first drawback and the pick's `why` ("no wealth tax below about €3.7M") agree. Agrees with ES_ANDALUSIA and ITSGF_LEVEL in src/data/localTaxes.ts (0% to €700k + €3M, then 1.7% / 2.1% / 3.5% at the state breakpoints).

claims.claim: Madrid's relief is reduced by the solidarity tax, so residents pay nothing up to about €3.7M of net wealth and about 1.7–3.5% above

sources.name: Comunidad de Madrid: Impuesto sobre el Patrimonio
sources.says: Last updated 12 May 2026. The personal minimum is 700.000 €. Madrid has had "una bonificación del 100 por ciento" since 2008; while the ITSGF is in force "no será aplicable la bonificación general del 100 por ciento" and the bonus is the difference between the wealth-tax quota and the ITSGF quota, so ITSGF taxpayers in effect pay wealth tax and their ITSGF is 0.

sources.name: Agencia Tributaria: Manual práctico de Patrimonio 2025, bonificaciones autonómicas, Madrid
sources.says: General bonus "100 por 100 de la cuota minorada"; while the ITSGF is in force it is replaced by the difference, if any, between the wealth-tax quota and the ITSGF quota (disposición transitoria séptima and article 20 of the Texto Refundido, Decreto Legislativo 1/2010), still applicable in 2025.

sources.name: PwC: Spain, other taxes
sources.says: Solidarity tax: EUR 700,000 exemption; 0% to 3,000,000 of base, 1.7% to 5,347,998.03, 2.1% to 10,695,996.06, 3.5% above. Last reviewed 30 June 2026.

claims.note: "Nothing between €700k and about €3.7M" is right, and nothing is due below €700k either. The summary ("no wealth tax between €700k and about €3.7M"), the second drawback and the pick's `why` agree. Agrees with ES_MADRID in src/data/localTaxes.ts.

claims.claim: Catalonia's wealth tax starts above a €500k exemption

sources.name: Agencia Tributaria: Manual práctico de Patrimonio 2025, mínimo exento, residentes en comunidades autónomas
sources.says: Cataluña: "el importe del mínimo exento se fija en 500.000 euros." Where a region sets none, "la base imponible se reducirá en 700.000 euros". Comunitat Valenciana (2025): 1.000.000 euros.

sources.name: Guía Fiscal: Patrimonio 2026, mapa de bonificaciones por comunidad
sources.says: Cataluña: mínimo exento 500,000 €, below the general 700,000 €; bonificación 0%; scale 0.21% to 3.48%; wealth tax paid in Catalonia is deducted from the ITSGF quota.

claims.note: The Catalan tax agency's own page was not found by search (atc.gencat.cat); the state agency's manual is official and current for 2025, and the secondary page gives the same figure for 2026. Agrees with ES_CATALONIA in src/data/localTaxes.ts. The summaries, the first drawbacks and both `why` lines ("wealth tax from €500k") agree. scores.tax stays 1.

claims.claim: The Catalan scale runs from 0.21% to 3.48%, with no relief

sources.name: Agencia Tributaria: Manual práctico de Patrimonio 2025, escala autonómica de Cataluña
Guía Fiscal: Patrimonio 2026, mapa de bonificaciones por comunidad
sources.says: Cataluña: bonificación 0% ("no bonus has been considered"); scale 0.21% to 3.48%.

claims.modelMismatch: ES_CATALONIA in src/data/localTaxes.ts uses the state breakpoints (ES_STEPS) for the Catalan scale, so its fifth band starts at €1,336,999.51 of base; the Catalan scale in the Agencia Tributaria's 2025 manual starts that band at €1,336,999.75 (page: .../patrimonio-2025/.../escalas-autonomicas/comunidad-autonoma-cataluna.html). A 24-cent difference with no effect on results. Every rate (0.21, 0.315, 0.525, 0.945, 1.365, 1.785, 2.205, 2.75, 3.48), the other breakpoints, the €500k exemption and the €20M start of the top band match the model.

claims.claim: The Catalan wealth tax is credited against the national solidarity tax

sources.name: PwC: Spain, other taxes
sources.says: The solidarity tax is complementary to wealth tax: "the wealth tax debt paid in relation to the same tax period should be deducted from the solidarity tax amount." Last reviewed 30 June 2026.

sources.name: Guía Fiscal: Patrimonio 2026, mapa de bonificaciones por comunidad
sources.says: Cataluña: wealth tax paid is deducted from the ITSGF quota, so the state tax applies only to the difference.

claims.note: Tarragona's profile does not state it; it applies there too. The same credit is why the Valencian profiles need no solidarity-tax line: with a €2M exemption the Valencian tax still exceeds the solidarity tax at every level worked through (e.g. about €21,300 against €5,100 at €4M of net wealth), which agrees with the model note "adds little on top".

claims.claim: Spain's inheritance tax is charged on the heir

sources.name: BOE: Ley 29/1987 del Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones, consolidated text
sources.says: Article 5: in acquisitions "mortis causa" the taxpayers are "los causahabientes". Consolidated text last updated 10 July 2021.

sources.name: PwC: Spain, other taxes
sources.says: Inheritance tax is levied on goods and rights "acquired by Spanish tax residents by inheritance, legacy or other type of succession"; liability depends on the relationship to the deceased and the heir's prior wealth. Last reviewed 30 June 2026.

claims.claim: A non-resident heir is taxed only on assets located in Spain, so US assets left to US-resident children appear to fall outside the tax

sources.name: BOE: Ley 29/1987 del Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones, consolidated text
sources.says: Article 6: residents are taxed "por obligación personal, con independencia de dónde se encuentren situados los bienes". Article 7: others are taxed by obligación real on assets "que estuvieran situados, pudieran ejercitarse o hubieran de cumplirse en territorio español". Additional provision 2 (Uno, 1.b): where the deceased lived in an autonomous community, "los contribuyentes no residentes tendrán derecho a la aplicación de la normativa propia" of that community.

sources.name: PwC: Spain, other taxes
sources.says: Non-residents are taxed on goods located, exercisable or to be fulfilled in Spain; the rules were reformed from 1 January 2015 after the EU Court of Justice judgment of 3 September 2014. Last reviewed 30 June 2026.

claims.note: What the profiles call an inference is the plain reading of articles 6 and 7: the test is the heir's residence, not the deceased's, and a US-resident child inheriting shares of US companies held at a US broker acquires nothing located in Spain. The profiles' "appear" and "(an inference; confirm with a Spanish adviser)" stay; they do no harm. No page read addresses the situs of each asset type (for example cash in a Spanish bank account or Spanish property, which the same child would be taxed on, with the right to the deceased's region's reliefs). Which region's rule applies: for heirs, resident or not, it is the region where the deceased lived, not where the heir lives. Agrees with ES_HEIR_NOTE in src/data/localTaxes.ts. scores.estate stays 4 in all seven: the rubric takes a point off where the reach is "only inferred, not confirmed". With the statute now read, the user may judge it confirmed and score 5; not changed here, since no fact was corrected.

sources.says: Comunitat Valenciana: "Reducción en base de 100.000 € + bonificación 99 %" for groups I and II; a child inheriting €200,000 pays 0.00 €. Updated 1 November 2026.

claims.oldWording: a resident heir gets a €1M reduction plus 99% relief in Andalusia
claims.newWording: a resident child gets a €1M reduction plus 99% relief in Andalusia

sources.says: Last updated 12 November 2026. A "bonificación del 99%" of the inheritance and gift tax quota for transfers between parents and children and between spouses; since 1 July 2025 the bonus for group III relatives (siblings, uncles, nephews) is 50%.

sources.says: Spouses and stable partners: "una bonificació del 99 % de la quota tributària". Other group II taxpayers: a table of 11 rows, 60% on the first 100,000 € of base, then marginal 55%, 50%, 45%, 40%, 35%, 30%, 25%, 20%, 10% and 0% above 3,000,000 € (average 28.92% at 3,000,000 €). sources.name: Agència Tributària de Catalunya: herències, reduccions i base liquidable
sources.says: Kinship reduction, group II: "Fill/a: 100.000 €."

claims.claim: EU PRIIPs rules block new buys of US-listed ETFs

sources.name: LYNX: Key Information Document (help page of a broker whose accounts are carried by Interactive Brokers)
sources.says: Retail clients are "not permitted to trade ETFs or other products that do not have a valid KID"; many non-EU ETFs have none. Can a retail client buy US ETFs? "No, not unless you are classified as a professional investor." The same applies to ETFs from Canada, Hong Kong, Mexico and Australia. The KID has applied to most products since 1 January 2018.

sources.name: Banker on Wheels: Interactive Brokers review
sources.says: Last updated 2 November 2026. "PRIIPs is an EU rule that prohibits buying US-listed ETFs", and this also applies to UK investors; US ETFs are open only to elective professional clients, while UCITS ETFs are available to all Europeans.

claims.note: The profiles' "reportedly" stays; it does no harm.

claims.claim: The block is on buying, not on holding US-listed ETFs

sources.name: LYNX: Key Information Document (help page of a broker whose accounts are carried by Interactive Brokers)
sources.says: The page's FAQ says retail clients "may still hold or sell existing positions, but new purchases are restricted."

sources.name: Regulation (EU) No 1286/2014, Article 13, as adopted (legislation.gov.uk copy of the EU text)
sources.says: The duty to provide a KID falls on "a person advising on, or selling, a PRIIP" before the retail investor is bound; nothing in the article reaches a PRIIP the investor already holds or a sale by the investor.

sources.says: Requires a "Document accrediting effective residence in Spain for a continuous period of at least one year" and registration in a municipality; "monthly fee of 60 euros" under 65 and "monthly fee of 157 euros" at 65 or over; gives the SNS basic common basket of benefits.
